note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

precepts.why:
Sirach says “The fear of the Lord driveth away sins”. Why? Because a person that fears God is going to keep the commandments and uphold the integrity to do the right thing, whatever situation or inconvenience he is in. Our integrity, our moral character, is directly tied to our fear toward God. It is one and the same.

Chapter 18 shows that fear at work: “A wise man will fear in every thing”. That is integrity guiding you in every step. Every step you are asking, is this the right move to make? Is this in alignment with the laws of God?

“And in the day of sinning he will beware of offence”, because he is examining himself. He has the fear of God in him and he is walking in his integrity. “But a fool will not observe time.”

The same goes for moments of correction. If you are dealing with the leadership and you cannot take the correction, if you are unable to digest it, understand it, take it and receive it, that is a sign of where your faith and your belief are.

So we have to make sure we are walking in the fear of the Lord. That fear is “the root of wisdom”, and where it is present it drives away sin and “turneth away wrath.”

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

precepts.why:
“Exalt not thyself, lest thou fall, and bring dishonour upon thy soul, and so God discover thy secrets, and cast thee down in the midst of the congregation, because thou camest not in truth to the fear of the Lord, but thy heart is full of deceit.”

Abimelech exalted himself and took the throne as if he had earned it, but he came not in truth, and his heart was full of deceit. God discovered the secret that he had slain his brothers and cast him down in the midst of the congregation: a piece of a millstone on his head at Thebez, his skull broken, dying by his own armourbearer's sword. Killing his seventy brothers bought him a three year reign and a crushed skull; it was to no profit.

precepts.text: Godliness is an abomination to a sinner; that is why Saul became David's enemy continually.
precepts.point: The princes of the Philistines went forth, and David behaved himself more wisely than all the servants of Saul, so that his name was much set by; harmless as a dove, wise as a serpent.

note.label: 1 Samuel 18: The Envious Eye of Saul

precepts.why:
“The parables of knowledge are in the treasures of wisdom: but godliness is an abomination to a sinner.” That is why “Saul became David’s enemy continually.”

Put the verses together: “Saul saw and knew that the Lord was with David”, and he chose to be that man's enemy anyway. If you know the Lord is with somebody and you make yourself their enemy, you have made yourself the adversary.

David was righteous, obedient and humble; Saul was envious, wicked and rebellious, and he could not stand him. As sin is an abomination to the Most High, so godliness is an abomination to a sinner: the sinner cannot bear to look at righteousness.

precepts.text: The fear of the Most High to keep his commandments was created in the elect from the womb.
precepts.point: All who heard were amazed, asking if this is not the same man who destroyed those who called on Christ's name. But Saul increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. He already knew the scriptures under Gamaliel; when Christ was revealed, everything started to make sense and he took it to another level.
precepts.why:
“To fear the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.” The fear of the Most High to keep his commandments was created in the elect from the womb.

That is what was in Saul, separated from his mother's womb. He had the scriptures under Gamaliel, and when Christ was revealed, that fear created in him from the womb took it to another level, so he increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews.

Thou camest not in truth to the fear of the Lord. The Lord seeketh such to worship him in spirit and truth. You are faking it in the sight of men. You are walking as a hypocrite. You are teaching the word of God, but you are not applying the word of God. You make merchandise out of the people. You use them, you abuse them. points: To fear the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb. To fear the Lord is the beginning of your wise understanding. To fear the Lord means to understand that there are judgments, repercussions for wrongdoing or sin. That shows a level of wisdom, because it gives you that discernment: let me not do this, because this is the repercussion if I do it. So fearing the Lord is the beginning of that overall wisdom, to understand how things operate, why it is in perfect order, why the Lord created judgments. Because he created laws that you were not allowed to break, and all of that starts to make sense.

And it was created with the faithful in the womb. Now that is super heavy. There are a couple of sisters in here with children in the womb. The Bible says the Lord already ordained, from that child being in that womb, that it is faithful enough to have the wisdom of the Lord upon delivery. Before the child is born, the Lord already ordained some things. There is none of you in here by happenstance. I know some of you think that you stumbled on a YouTube video, that you walked by the camp that day, that you were going somewhere else. You did not stumble on anything.
If thou desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the Lord shall give her unto thee. Keeping the commandments is an action. This is our foundation; this is the integrity we roll by.

When you are keeping the commandments with all your heart and all your soul, you really have no choice but to have very good integrity, and a person keeping them willfully will have very good character. You cannot keep the commandments with all your heart and have horrible character; it makes no sense.
